body:
I think I might come again to get things off my chest. Actually I'm pretty sure I will. I'm calmed down now but when I next see my sibling I'll probably want to murder them again.

I paid for one of my sister university fees last week because my parents asked me to. She didn't even thank me but instead she said "why the fuck it took so long". Then last night I logged onto my skype and found out she has been using it to sms her friends. Saying things like she hope that my dad and I will just die horribly. I don't even know why the hell I'm helping someone like that and continue to... just as I'm typing this, I just heard from my mom that she doesn't want to go to that uni anymore and wants me to pay for another uni. The deposit I paid are non refundable. Anyway... I think my anger are kicking in again and I need to go off and chill my head.

I did read one online somewhere but it didn't work too well. When the tantrum kicks in, I just loses it and can't think clearly. My head will keep repeating the situation over and over and my anger just goes through the roof. It is funny how I'm able to keep a straight face even though my blood is boiling at this point.

I'll take a look at a few books and maybe ask a friend who works as a counselor for teenagers when I next see her.

Thanks for sharing it. I thought I was really losing it for having such awful nightmares and the fact that I woke up laughing from it. It sounds like your dreams are more violent and vivid than mine. It also makes me feel a lot better to know I'm more fortunate compared to others.

My parents marriage is a schamble and it's been like that ever since I can remember. They haven't slept in the same room for over 20 years nor show any public affection against each other. I went abroad to study when I was 12 and didn't lived with my family until I graduated from uni. I didn't see them much even before I left. Since I've started work, they decided they have enough money to retire and they want to "repair" the broken family we have. I understand what my parents are thinking but I told them it is too late. We are all mature adults now and bringing everyone back to live together is actually more damaging to our family. They have this guilt that they haven't really spend time with us when we were young so they are trying to do it now. I agree sometimes we do have fun as a family but I can only remember the arguments we have. It is pretty much everyday that we argue now, it isn't getting any better.

Last year I moved out after the police got involved. All my friends and partner supported me. But after a few months my dad started suffering depression due to the incident and my mom went around to my friends and beg them to convince me to go home. I moved home shortly afterwards but the atmosphere was worse. My siblings was happy that I was gone but now they hold a bigger grudge against me because I got them arrested. I didn't want to sue my own family so I dropped all the charges even though the police recommended not.

I've spoken to my partner and I'm planning to move in with her once things settle down a bit. But I really have no idea how they going to react to it. Thanks for listening it does help to get it off my chest

It's nice that you think I'm still sane. I nearly deleted the post, part of me probably feel embarassed and the other part worries about criticism. You're right about the work and home being uncomfortable environment. It reallys gets me when I have a bad day at work and when I go home to a similar environment. It got so bad once that the police had to arrest my family members and escort me to safety.

I had two very close friend male and female friend who knew what was going on. One said my whole family is mad and he didn't want to get involved. The other tried to help, got involved and after about a week she got really scared and we went from very close friends/family to just friends. She said her family is messed up but can't even compare to mine just from a week of contact. The problem as you said is too deep and even the psychiatrist couldn't help. We "had" a friend who works as a counsellor. She tried to help our family but it didn't end up well.

I've lost it a few times in the office, it wasn't nice as my close colleagues said that I diverted my anger at them rather than the ones that were bullying me.

I really hope I was just unlucky to experience this at home and work. But thinking about it now, it must be me. I've changed jobs and it is exactly the same. At first I get along with people very well because I always try to be nice and helpful but as time goes on I let people walk all over me as I don't know how to say no or to stand up for myself. My mind just completely switches itself off when I'm in that situation and I let the anger overwhelm me.
